question: The European Union has included journalist Hüseyin Doğru in its sanctions regime, completely freezing his financial resources without there being criminal charges, a prior hearing or an effective judicial review.

Such an action limits his freedom of movement, makes it impossible for him to exercise his profession and leaves him defenceless, which demonstrates the use of sanctions as a tool of political repression and persecution.

The sanctions not only affect Doğru, but have also been extended to his family environment: his wife’s bank accounts were recently frozen, which transfers the sanction to a person who is not included on any EU list. Those actions are in line with the logic of authoritarian regimes and leave citizens unprotected.

The use of sanctions to punish or deter critical journalistic activity, especially in the face of reports of human rights violations, runs counter to the EU’s founding values. In view of the above: 1.
How does the Commission ensure that sanctions regimes are not used as tools of political repression that violate fundamental rights?
What action will the Commission take to protect the individuals concerned and their families from disproportionate sanctions by Member States such as Germany?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.5.2026) Mr Huseyin Dogru has been listed under the Russia destabilising activities restrictive measures regime since 20 May 20251. The reasons for listing him are public and contained in the Annex to the relevant legal acts.

As such, he is subject to an asset freeze and prohibition to make funds available, as well as to a travel ban, as per Articles 1 and 2 of Council Decision (CFSP) 2024/26432 and Article 2 of Council Regulation (EU) 2024/26423 concerning restrictive measures in view of Russia’s destabilising activities.

As per the above-mentioned articles, the asset freeze applies to ‘all funds and economic resources belonging to, owned, held or controlled by’ a listed person. The implementation of EU restrictive measures is the responsibility of the Member States.

As per the provisions in the legal acts, every listed person has a right to ask the competent authorities in a Member State to unfreeze assets necessary to satisfy the basic needs of the listed person and their family members, such as payments for foodstuffs, rent or mortgage, medicines and medical treatment, and other necessary expenses.

Mr Huseyin Dogru, as every other person subject to sanctions, has the right to make representations to the Council, request his delisting, bring a legal challenge and contest the listing before the EU courts. The EU courts are independent and ensure that any listing is lawful.
1 Council Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/965 of 20 May 2025 implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2642

concerning restrictive measures in view of Russia’s destabilising activities (OJ L, 2025/965, 20.5.2025, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2025/965/oj). Council Decision (CFSP) 2025/966 of 20 May 2025 amending Decision (CFSP) 2024/2643 concerning restrictive measures in view of Russia’s destabilising activities http://data.europa.eu/eli/dec/2025/966/oj.

2 Council Decision (CFSP) 2024/2643 of 8 October 2024 concerning restrictive measures in view of Russia’s destabilising activities http://data.europa.eu/eli/dec/2024/2643/2026-03-16. 3 Council Regulation (EU) 2024/2642 of 8 October 2024 concerning restrictive measures in view of Russia’s destabilising activities http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/2642/2026-03-16.
